children: Activity in Sweden's manufacturing sector increased marginally in August, with the Purchasing Managers' Index rising to 56.1 points from 55.7 points in July, compilers Silf and Swedbank said on Tuesday.
The sub-index for production was the biggest contributor to the rise. The sub-index for orders gave a negative contribution.

Prices for a wide range of input goods rose in August, including energy commodities, metals, plastics, electronic products, as well as transportation costs pushing the sub-index for goods up to 75.5 points from 67.2 points.

"The growing cost pressures mean that industrial companies are facing increasing challenges from higher raw material prices and disruptions in global supply chains. If this trend persists, the risk of both squeezed profit margins and higher inflationary pressures going forward will increase," Swedbank economist Jorgen Kennemar said in a statement.
